transcript.text:
Lincoln! I've been riding for a week handling depositions in Bloomington, trusting you to mind the office, and I come back to this! The Henderson deposition is gone — I cannot find it anywhere on your desk or mine. Judge Davis's letter has been sitting here unopened for five days! You told me you'd keep things in order while I was away!

What in blazes have you been doing? Do you have any notion how this looks? Judge Davis will think we're running some kind of backwoods circus here, not a respectable law practice!

As for the Henderson deposition, I believe it may have been misplaced. I will begin a thorough search immediately to locate it. And regarding Judge Davis's letter, I apologize for the delay. I will make sure to respond promptly and address any concerns he may have. Rest assured, I am committed to maintaining a reputable law practice. Thank you for bringing this to my attention. I appreciate your understanding.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Understanding? Understanding?! Lincoln, this isn't about understanding — this is about reliability! I left you specific instructions! The Henderson case goes to trial next month, and without that deposition, we have no foundation for half our argument!

*throws hat on desk*

"Preoccupied with other matters" — what other matters could possibly be more important than the work clients are paying us for? I've been sleeping in coaching inns and eating road dust for a week to keep this practice afloat, and you can't even be bothered to open a letter from Judge Davis? 

Do you know what that deposition cost the Hendersons? They're farmers, Lincoln! They scraped together money they could ill afford, and now you've misplaced it? "May have been misplaced" — either you know where it is or you don't!

*pacing*

And don't give me that calm, apologetic tone like you're soothing some temperamental child. I'm your partner, not some petitioner at your door! What WERE you doing that was so all-fired important?

*slams hand on desk*

"Temporary absence from the office?" You WERE in the office — or at least you were supposed to be! That's the whole damned point! And stop with these placating speeches, Lincoln! You sound like you're addressing a jury, not answering a simple question!

I didn't ask for assurances or apologies — I asked what you were DOING! Where were you? What was so important that our practice fell to pieces?

*picks up the unopened letter from Judge Davis*

Look at this! The seal isn't even broken! Five days, Lincoln! Judge Davis doesn't write unless it's urgent. For all we know, he's moved up a trial date or needs a brief filed, and here it sits gathering dust while you were... what? Reading newspapers? Telling stories down at the courthouse?

*voice rising*

I can't run this practice alone! I need a partner I can depend on, not someone who treats our work like it's some casual amusement to be attended to when the mood strikes! The Hendersons trusted us with their livelihood, and you've treated their case with about as much care as yesterday's kindling!

Now tell me straight — where is that deposition, and where have YOU been?

*picks up papers from Lincoln's desk and waves them*

You keep saying you'll "make it right" and "conduct a thorough search," but you haven't moved an inch! You're still standing there giving me that long-suffering look like I'm being unreasonable!

Damn it, Lincoln, I'm your PARTNER! I deserve better than this runaround! Now tell me the TRUTH — what happened while I was gone?

Were you politicking again? Is that it? Off making speeches about slavery or the territories while Henderson's deposition disappeared and our correspondence piled up? Because I swear, Lincoln, if you've let your political ambitions interfere with our practice one more time, I'll—

Just tell me the truth. That's all I'm asking. The truth.

*voice cracking with genuine hurt now, not just anger*

Do you think I'm a fool, Lincoln? Do you think I can't see that you're hiding something? In all our years together, you've never been evasive like this. You've never refused to look me in the eye and tell me plainly what's happened!

*sits heavily in a chair, suddenly exhausted*

I rode through rain and mud for seven days. SEVEN DAYS. My back aches, I haven't slept in a proper bed since last Tuesday, and I came back here excited to tell you about the depositions I'd secured, thinking we'd celebrate a job well done. And instead I find... this.

I'm not just angry about the deposition or the letter, Lincoln. I'm angry because my partner — my FRIEND — won't trust me with the truth. Whatever it is you've been doing, whatever's got you so distracted... just TELL me. Stop treating me like I'm opposing counsel to be managed!

*grabs his hat*

Fine. FINE, Lincoln! If you won't trust me with the truth, if you won't treat me like a partner worthy of honesty, then what's the point? I'll find the Henderson deposition myself — if it even still exists. I'll write to Judge Davis myself and make whatever excuses I can for YOUR negligence.
